title: Claude Enterprise Pricing: Plans, Seats & Costs (2026)
summary: Claude Enterprise pricing from Anthropic isn't publicly listed, but here's what deployment typically costs companies by feature tier and volume.
body_markdown:
## What Activepieces does about this


The part of this bill that seat pricing handles worst is repetitive machine work, and that is where Activepieces fits.


It is an automation platform that can call Claude through the API from a workflow, so a job like summarizing every support ticket runs on metered usage and never occupies a person's seat or eats into their limits.


The seat stays with the people who ask varied, one-off questions.


The pricing model suits that split. A run counts as 1 credit however many steps it has, and unlimited flows come on every plan, including the free one.


So adding a workflow doesn't add a line item, and the number you budget is how often the work runs.


On Plus and up you can attach your own AI provider key, which puts the model cost on your provider bill, where you can see it and set your own spending alerts.


You then price that usage by the same pilot-and-measure method this article recommends for seats.


You can check the claims before you commit. The credit structure is published on the Activepieces pricing page, and the free plan lets you build a ticket-summary flow and count its runs against your pilot.


Alan and Funding Societies run production automation on Activepieces, so this isn't a toy for scripts that nobody depends on.


What it doesn't change is the Claude contract. Seat minimums, caps and overage terms still come from Anthropic sales, in writing.


Moving the repetitive jobs elsewhere shrinks the number of seats you need to defend and keeps your heaviest automated usage out of the extra usage billing that heavy seat users trigger.
